sentences.text: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.10,50,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 17-09-2023, in the early morning between 2.00 a.m. to 2.10 a.m., the petitioner along with his brother Rishav Tanuk and his friend by name Suyesh was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KK-6021, near Sanjaynagar 80 feet road.

When they reached near 4th cross, Sanjaynagar, at that time the driver of Suzuki Wagon R VXI car bearing Reg. No.TN-66-AE-1800 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly turned to the right side without any indication.

The petitioner,
whose motorcycle was behind the car, could not avoid his motorcycle colliding with the said car on its right side and dashed to another car bearing No.KA-03-AD-0461,
which was parked on the side of the road.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner along with his brother and friend fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to M.S.
Ramaiah Memorial Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took first aid treatment and was kept under observation.
Earlier to the accident he was working as Freelancing Event Manager and earning a sum of Rs.50,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.

The R.T. Nagar Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C. The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.

Hence,
they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore,
it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.10,50,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Section 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.

It has denied for having insured the Suzuki Wagon R VXI car bearing Reg.
No.TN-66-AE-1800 and it is subject to confirmation from the concerned branch of this respondent and the liability of this respondent if any is subject to terms, conditions and limitations of policy of insurance, issued in favour of the respondent No.2 and in accordance with the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that, the car bearing No.TN-66-AE-1800 was being driven by its driver without possessing valid and effective driving licence, permit and fitness Aditya C Parmar vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78177357/
2 certificate, as on the date of the alleged accident.

sentences.text: As there is breach of terms and conditions of the policy, this respondent is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.2.

Further it is contended that,
the petitioner was pillion rider of the motorcycle, totally 3 persons were traveling on the bike.
Due to over load they fell down on the road at 2.00 a.m. in midnight.
The time goes to show that, the rider and pillion riders were under influence of the alcohol.
Hence, rider has lost control over the bike and hit to the car bearing No.TN-66-AE-1800 and thereafter hit to the another car bearing No.KA-03-AD-0461.
More over all are under teenage, they were not wearing helmet and did not hold driving licence and insurance policy with respect to said motorcycle.
Hence, the alleged has taken place due to negligence on the part of the rider of motorcycle and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of car bearing No.TN-66-AE-1800.
Further it is contended that, the driver of the Omni car had also contributed to the cause of alleged accident and was guilty of contributory negligence.
All three vehicles have got damaged on the front portion and the accident has taken place in the junction.
Hence, all the three vehicles have caused the accident.
But, the petitioner has not made the owner and insurer of said vehicles as party to the present proceedings.
The owner and insurer of car bearing No.KA-03-AD-0461 (LMV) and owner and insurer of motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KK-6021 are necessary party to the present proceedings.

Further it has denied the age,
income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by the petitioner.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. Whereas, the respondent No.2 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
He has contended that, he is the registered owner of the car bearing No.TN-66-AE-1800 and the said car was insured with respondent No.1 and the said policy was valid from 25-06- 2023 to 24-06-2024.
Further it is contended that, his son who was driving the said car was holding valid driving licence and the vehicle was covered with valid insurance policy, at the time of alleged accident.
Further it is contended that, he has not violated any terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
At the time of accident the driver of offending vehicle was driving the same with great care and caution.

There was a contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner, as three persons were riding on the said two-wheeler, which was permissible for only two persons and they were not wearing helmet which is contravention of law.
Further it is contended that, at the time of accident the offending vehicle was insured by the respondent No.1 insurance company.
As such, the respondent No.2 is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
For the above denials and contentions, he has prayed to dismiss the petition.

6. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 17-09-2023 at about 2.00 a.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Suzuki Wagon R VXI Car bearing Reg. No.TN-66-AE- Aditya C Parmar vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78177357/
3 1800 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
7. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 18 documents as Ex.P.1 to 18.
On the other hand, the respondents No.1 and 2 have not adduced any evidence on their behalf.
8. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

In support of his arguments, the learned counsel for petitioner has relied on the following decisions:
i. Mohammed Siddique and another V/s National Insurance Company Limited and others, reported in (2020) 3 SCC 57.

My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Partly Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 17-09-2023, in between 2.00 a.m. to 2.10 a.m., when he along with his brother Rishav Tanuk and his friend by name Suyesh was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04- KK-6021, near Sanjaynagar 80 feet road and

when they were reached near 4th Cross, Sanjaynagar, at that time the driver of offending Suzuki Wagon R VXI car bearing Reg. No.TN-66-AE-1800 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly turned to the right side, without any indication.

Due to which, the petitioner, whose motorcycle was behind the car, could not avoid colliding his motorcycle to the said car on its right side and dashing to another car bearing No.KA-03-AD-0461, which was parked on the side of the road.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner along with his brother and friend fell on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident he was working as Freelancing Event Manager and earning a sum of Rs.50,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
11. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 18 documents as Ex.P.1 to 18.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of police notice, Ex.P.4 is true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.5 is true copy of sketch, Ex.P.6 is true copy of notice under Section 133 of Motor Vehicles Act, Ex.P.7 is true Aditya C Parmar vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78177357/
4 copy of reply to notice under Section 133 of Motor Vehicles Act, Ex.P.8 is true copy of indemnity bond, Ex.P.9 is true copy of Motor Vehicles Accident report, Ex.P.10 to 12 are true copy of wound certificates of Rishav, Suresh and Aditya, Ex.P.13 is discharge summary, Ex.P.14 are medical bills (total 12), Ex.P.15 are prescriptions (total 5), Ex.P.16 are photos (total 5), Ex.P.17 is C.D. and Ex.P.18 is true copy of charge-sheet.

12. On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 12 and 18,
prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.TN-66-AE-1800 and suddenly turning the same to the right side without giving any indication.

Due to which, the petitioner who was riding his motorcycle behind the said car could not avoid colliding with the said car on its right side and then dashed to another car bearing No.KA- 03-AD-0461, which was parked on the side of the road.
Due to said impact the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained simple injuries.

The investigation officer in his final report/charge-sheet, which is marked as Ex.P.18, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg.
No.TN-66-AE-1800 and the petitioner has sustained simple injuries in the said accident.
13.

At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.1 in respect of car bearing Reg.
No.TN-66-AE-1800 and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

But, the respondent No.1 & 2 have specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KK-6021 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of car bearing Reg. No.TN-66-AE-1800.

Further it is contended that, the petitioner in collusion with the police authorities and owner of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KK-6021 has got registered a false case against the driver of car bearing Reg.
No.TN-66-AE-1800, to get wrongful gain from the respondents.
But, the respondents have failed to establish the said contentions.

They have neither adduced any evidence, nor they have produced any document to show that, the said accident has taken place solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KK-6021 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of car bearing Reg. No.TN-66-AE-1800.
Even the respondents have not stepped into witness box to depose the said contentions on oath.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg.
No.TN-66-AE- 1800 and suddenly turning the same to the right side without any indication.

Due to which, the petitioner who was riding his motorcycle behind the said car could not avoid colliding with the said car on its right side and dashing the same to another car bearing No.KA-03-AD- 0461,
which was parked on the side of the road.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross- examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04- KK-6021 or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

sentences.text: But, it is pertinent to note that, admittedly, at the time of accident the petitioner/rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KK-6021 was riding the same along with two pillion riders.

There are every chances that, due to three persons traveling on a motorcycle, which is meant for two persons,
there would be congestion to the petitioner/rider of said motorcycle and he might have lost control resulting in the accident.
The petitioner has taken risk of riding the said motorcycle along with two pillion riders.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner/rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KK-6021 is also liable for contributory negligence in the cause of accident.

But, as there is no evidence on record to show that, the very act of three persons riding on the motorcycle has directly contributed either to the accident or to the impact of the accident upon the victim, this Court is of the opinion that, holding the petitioner/rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KK-6021 liable for contributory negligence to the extent of 10% would be justified and will meet the ends of justice.

15. The Ex.P.4 spot mahazar and Ex.P.5 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the right side of the road, near 4th cross, 80 feet road, Sanjaynagara, Bengaluru, in between the offending car bearing Reg. No.TN-66-AE-1800 and motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KK- 6021 of the petitioner.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.9, the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident is not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.18 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.TN-66-AE-1800 and the petitioner has sustained simple injuries in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.TN-66-AE-1800.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

16. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.12 wound certificate and Ex.P.13 discharge summary it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered simple injuries in the road traffic accident.
The petitioner has sustained left knee open wound, abrasion over both hands and right leg.
On the other hand, there is no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record, to disbelieve the said medical records.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondent No.1 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg.
No.TN-66-AE-1800 and the petitioner has sustained simple injuries in the said accident.
17. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) 11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal Aditya C Parmar vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78177357/
6 case are not required."

18. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
19.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained injuries in a motor vehicle accident occurred on 17-09-2023 at about 2:00 a.m., near 4th cross, 80 feet road, Sanjaynagara, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.TN-66-AE-1800.
But, the petitioner has failed to prove that, he has sustained grievous injury in the said accident.
As per the Ex.P.12 wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained simple injuries.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Partly Affirmative.
20. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.TN-66-AE-1800 and he has sustained simple injuries in the said accident.
The petitioner has sustained left knee open wound, abrasion over both hands and right leg.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.
But, there is absolutely no evidence placed on record by the petitioner to show that, he has suffered any disability or deformity due to above injuries.
The petitioner has neither examined any doctor, nor he has produced any document for the purpose of assessing the above pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to award global compensation in general.
21. As per Ex.P.12 wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained left knee open wound, abrasion over both hands and right leg.
The above said injuries are simple in nature.
As per Ex.P.13 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for one day on 17-09-2023, in Ramaiah Memorial Hospital, Bengaluru.
The petitioner has deposed that, he has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards medicine, conveyance, attendant charges and nourishment.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 12 medical bills, as per Ex.P.14.

All the bills have been examined carefully and found that,
the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.13,482/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.13,482/- under the head medical expenses.

22. Further, the petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, earlier to the accident he was working as Freelancing Event Manager and earning a sum of Rs.50,000/- per month and due to the accidental injuries he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.

But,
the petitioner has failed to prove the same.

The petitioner has neither examined the doctor, nor he has produced any document to show that, he has suffered any permanent physical disability or Aditya C Parmar vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78177357/
7 deformity due to injuries sustained in the accident.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: No doubt, due to above injuries the petitioner might have suffered some pain and sufferings and the same would have been nourished with medicines, nutritious food and he might have spent some money for conveyance.

In such circumstances, taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case and the nature of injuries and treatment provided to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, some reasonable compensation is required to be awarded to the petitioner.
Accordingly, it it held that, awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/- to the petitioner, including medical expenses, would meet the ends of justice.
23. For the reasons stated supra, the petitioner is held liable for contributory negligence to the extent of 10%.

After deducting the said value from the above compensation amount, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.45,000/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization.
24. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle bearing No.TN-66-AE-1800.

Further, as per the true copy of reply given by the owner of offending vehicle, to the notice issued by the investigation officer under Sec.133 of Motor Vehicles Act, which is marked as Ex.P.7, the driver of offending vehicle by name Gopikrishnan S/o P. Srinivasan was holding valid and effective driving licence bearing No.TN3820200004752 to drive the said vehicle and it was valid from 26-09-2020 to 27-12-2035.
The policy issued by the respondent No.1 bearing No.99179232311013666, in respect of offending car, was valid from 25-06-2023 to 24-06-2024.

As such, the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.1 in respect of offending vehicle was valid as on the date of accident i.e.
17-09-2023.
There is no evidence on record to show that, there is breach of any terms and conditions of the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.1.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.TN-66-AE-1800 the accident in question has occurred and the petitioner has sustained simple injuries in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.45,000/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.1, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
25. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.45,000/- (Rupees forty five thousand only), with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.

In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
